top5.title: Anthropic Makes Record Debut on Nasdaq
top5.description: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT, after pricing its IPO at 83 dollars per share. The company sold 980 million shares for about 81.3 billion dollars and must now answer to both its shareholders and its users.
top5.why: Anthropic’s record Nasdaq debut is a major validation of the AI investment cycle while exposing the company to public-market scrutiny over profitability and governance.

top5.title: U.S. restricts exports of AI chips to foreign data centers
top5.description: The U.S. Commerce Department restricted, effective November 19, exports of advanced AI chips to foreign data centers providing large-scale computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted countries.
top5.why: U.S. restrictions on advanced AI-chip exports to foreign data centers will reshape global compute access, supply chains and the competitive balance with China.

top5.title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for 4.5 Billion Dollars
top5.description: Palo Alto Networks will acquire Applied Compute for 4.5 billion dollars in stock to add tools for training and deploying customized open-weight AI models. The transaction is expected to close in the third fiscal quarter of 2027.
top5.why: Palo Alto Networks’ $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute signals that cybersecurity companies are moving aggressively into AI-model training and deployment infrastructure.

top5.title: Apple is developing an AI agent capable of controlling a Mac
top5.description: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent for Mac that can write code, browse the web, and control apps on the user’s behalf. It could launch as early as the end of next year.
top5.why: Apple’s planned Mac-controlling AI agent could materially change how users interact with software and intensify competition with Microsoft and Google in autonomous computing.

top5.title: Google books Blue Origin to launch AI satellites in 2029
top5.description: Blue Origin will launch satellites serving as data centers for Google in 2029 as part of the Suncatcher project. The mission will test networking AI chips and running machine-learning tasks in space.
top5.why: Google’s agreement with Blue Origin to test orbital AI data centers points to a potentially significant long-term shift in how hyperscalers obtain energy and deploy compute, despite the project’s early stage.
